workflows.name: Pull request merged
workflows.reason: Merge is not verified release completion or PM acceptance.

automationLimits: The canonical standard has three active semantic states: In Progress, Pending Review and In Review. This current example has no verified native Pending Review option, so circulating handoffs are blocked until an exact Project mapping is supplied; only the PM may request On Hold.
When no Issue is active and the PM has not named one, recommend up to three ready Backlog Issues and wait for explicit PM selection; never auto-select the next Issue.

Implementation uses a feature branch and linked PR; the PR-ready candidate receives the full Showcase, PM feedback/fixes stay on that candidate, and only exact approval authorizes merge and Issue closure. A later Issue requires an explicit PM call.

Release cycles use repository-local Canary/Alpha/Beta/Stable channel configuration: Stable is mandatory, every included phase runs its full Dev Pipeline and PM approval, and no direct write enters Stable. Build method, QA environments and release destinations require explicit PM/Agent agreement; phase names never infer infrastructure.

The Issue evidence records ordered QA turns, current and next owner/environment, exact candidate, suite and PM state, and cleanup. Assignee follows the current baton owner; do not infer owner from OS.
QA completion never auto-closes an Issue. All configured release and PM completion gates remain required.
Agents discover field and option identifiers at runtime instead of hard-coding GraphQL IDs.
Agents own lifecycle movement and immediately read every mutation back.
Project copy is preferred because GitHub does not expose complete view and built-in workflow authoring through the public CLI.
